_doc: A SKIN is the visual language of one topic: what a step, a win, a failure, a price, a list and a result LOOK like in that world. The reference reels skinned a GTA explainer as a game HUD (MISSION 1/4, MISSION FAILED, a route map, a weapon wheel, MISSION PASSED) and a skills explainer as a dev terminal with skill nodes. tools/overlay_director.mjs picks the skin by topic keywords (or style-packs/<id>/style.json overlay_skin, or --skin) and uses its words and device preferences. Add your own: id, match[], words{}, prefer{}, accent, vocabulary.

skins.vocabulary: Everything is a game interface: a mission header with a step counter, waypoints on a map for steps, a weapon wheel for a list of options, a loot counter for money, FAILED with a RETRY button for the problem, PASSED for the result.
Terminals, file trees, skill nodes joined by lines, stars and licence chips, a lines-of-code counter, a diff for before/after, green PASS and red FAIL.
A ticker strip, candlesticks, a big counter for every figure, red and green deltas, a price tag on every cost, falling bills for money made.
A lower-third for every name, a dated headline card with its source, a map pin for every place, a stamp for CONFIRMED or DEBUNKED.
A timeline with clips, phones with platform labels, a views counter that climbs, a comment thread, POSTED and FLOPPED stamps.
Notebook paper, hand-drawn circles and arrows, a sticker for the one word that matters, a diagram that builds line by line.
